items.text: Flatness and families
Flat morphism $X\to Y$: a nice family; the dimension of the fibres cannot jump.
Sums are disjoint and universal
$X=\coprod X_i$ is disjoint if the $u_i\colon X_i\to X$ are monomorphisms ($X_i\times_XX_i=X_i$) and
X_i\times_XX_j=\varnothing\ \text{(initial object)}\qquad(i\neq j)
The sum is universal if for every base change $X'\to X$:
\coprod_iX'_i\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ X',\qquad X'_i=X_i\times_XX'
Affine algebraic spaces over $K$: finite sums are disjoint and universal.
A=\prod A_i:\quad A_i\otimes_AA_j=0\ (i\neq j)\quad(\text{in }B:\ 1=e_i=0\text{ in the image})
A'=\prod_iA'_i,\qquad A'_i=A'/(1-e'_i)=A_i\otimes_AA'
\Bigl(\coprod_iX_i\Bigr)\times\Bigl(\coprod_jY_j\Bigr)=\coprod_{i,j}X_i\times Y_j\qquad(\text{distributivity})
I_{\mathcal C}=\coprod_{i\in I}e,\qquad I_{\mathcal C}\times J_{\mathcal C}=(I\times J)_{\mathcal C}
$I\mapsto I_{\mathcal C}$ commutes with finite products and fibre products, sends the final object to the final object: it is left exact.
$I$ a finite group: $I_K$ is an affine algebraic group (constant group).
I_K=V_{K^I},\qquad K^I=\{\text{maps }I\to K\}
I\times I\to I\ \leadsto\ K^I\to K^I\otimes K^I=K^{I\times I}\quad(\text{transpose})
Fibre products and spectra
$Y\to S$ a monomorphism: $\operatorname{Spec}Z=f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}Y)$, and $\operatorname{Spec}Z\to\operatorname{Spec}X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}S}\operatorname{Spec}Y$ is bijective.

The topology of $\operatorname{Spec}Z$ is induced by $\operatorname{Spec}X$ if $A\to C$ is surjective (closed immersion), or $A\to A_f$ (open), or a quotient $A/J$ followed by localisation $T^{-1}(A/J)$.
Intersection of subobjects of $S$ = fibre product over $S$: $\operatorname{Spec}(X\cap Y)=\operatorname{Spec}X\cap\operatorname{Spec}Y$.

Fibre at a point $y$ with $\kappa(y)=K'$: $Y=\operatorname{Spec}K'\to S$, $Z=X\times_SY$; $\operatorname{Spec}Z$ = the fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}X\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ over $y$, with the induced topology.
Closure of an image
\overline{\varphi(V(J))}=V\bigl(\varphi^{-1}(J)\bigr),\qquad \varphi\colon\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A,\ J\subset B
